I farm 14 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full 14 mu into winter wheat first and then the same 14 mu into summer maize after wheat harvest. I am 67 and only have a 2-person household, so I will keep the plan steady and practical instead of doing anything complicated. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on stable water at the key stages rather than gamble on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, keep fertilizer at a medium-to-high level, irrigate several times, and do rotary tillage because it is manageable for me and fits the local rotation. For maize, I will use hybrid seed for stronger yield, keep nitrogen a bit higher than wheat, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and continue with rotary tillage so I can turn the season quickly after wheat. I will keep pesticide use limited to what is needed for the usual weeds, insects, and diseases, because I want the crop protected but I do not want unnecessary cost.
